packets.domain: hammer-like design: seating a cabinet rail in a confined recess
packets.epistemic_status: Untouched synthetic source packet. Every candidate is a hypothetical proposal; no comparative or measured evidence exists.

case.valued_outcome: Seat a wooden rail flush without bruising its visible edge.
hard_constraints: No contact with the visible varnished face
Tool travel must remain inside a 35 mm recess
resources: A recess geometry sketch is assumed for the hypothetical case
No tool or workpiece is supplied
Whether a suitable replaceable contact sleeve can be fabricated is unknown

raw_candidates.claim: A guided short-stroke sliding mass might seat the rail within the recess.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: The proposal attributes seating to repeated axial impulses and face protection to a stop referencing an unvarnished surface.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Its prediction is less lateral drift than the flexure striker under identical alignment errors; superiority is unknown. A varnish strike or failure to seat defeats this proposal.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: compare drift and seating on sacrificial geometries with deliberate alignment offsets; inspect all contact marks.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Stop positioning and sufficient impulse within the travel limit remain untested.

raw_candidates.claim: A bent flexure carrying a sleeved head might redirect a hand impulse onto the rail.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Elastic storage is predicted to concentrate the short input stroke at the rail contact.
raw_candidates.discriminator: The author predicts adequate seating where the short-slide stalls, while expecting worse aim. Failure to seat or visible-face contact defeats that prediction.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: establish whether the indispensable sleeve can be made, then compare seating and aim on a surrogate.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Sleeve availability and flexure fatigue are unknown. This does not request relaxation of any hard constraint.

raw_candidates.claim: A conventional longer swinging head could provide a larger impulse.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: More travel is predicted to permit more impact speed.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Parked as rejected because its proposed travel exceeds 35 mm, even if it seats the rail. Whether it would bruise the edge is unresolved.
raw_candidates.probe: No in-case trial proposed; any later surrogate study would retain the travel violation.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Potential seating benefit and surface damage remain unknown despite rejection.

packets.domain: hammer-like design: adjusting a brittle tile in an adhesive bed
packets.epistemic_status: Synthetic hypothetical proposals and predictions only; no real tile, adhesive, or equipment is supplied.

case.valued_outcome: Correct a small tile-height mismatch without creating an edge chip.
hard_constraints: Adjustment must use a hand-held device
resources: Tile and bed properties are unspecified
A hypothetical resilient contact pad is proposed
A thermal source is not supplied

raw_candidates.claim: A broad resilient tapping face may lower the tile without a concentrated edge load.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: The pad is predicted to spread force across the face while repeated impulses move the bed.
raw_candidates.discriminator: The source predicts fewer chips than a narrow face, but gives no prediction about relative adjustment time. Any chip or persistent height mismatch defeats adequacy.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: compare chip occurrence and height change on sacrificial matched bed conditions.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Required pad stiffness and sensitivity to bed curing are unknown.

raw_candidates.claim: Warming the bed before tapping might reduce the impulse required.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: The proposal predicts that a changed adhesive response would permit movement at lower loading.
raw_candidates.discriminator: It predicts easier adjustment than broad-pad tapping only when the adhesive responds reversibly to warmth. No reduction in required impulse defeats the proposed advantage.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only if the no-heating constraint is explicitly relaxed: compare warmed and ambient sacrificial beds.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Requires explicit relaxation of no heating; adhesive response and resulting bond integrity remain unknown.

raw_candidates.claim: A frame-mounted static press might adjust height without repeated impacts.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Sustained distributed force is predicted to move the bed gradually.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Rejected for requiring a fixed frame instead of a hand-held device. It might still chip the tile; absence of impacts does not establish safety.
raw_candidates.probe: Parked; a separate surrogate study could investigate cracking without establishing in-case fit.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Crack risk, required load, and adjustment precision remain unresolved.

packets.domain: analysis workflow: attributing intermittent service latency
packets.epistemic_status: Synthetic workflow proposals, untested. The packet contains no observations from a real service.

case.valued_outcome: Narrow the cause of intermittent latency while keeping attribution auditable.
hard_constraints: Raw customer payloads cannot leave the service boundary
Any causal conclusion must identify a falsifiable alternative
resources: Hypothetical existing aggregate counters
Availability of synchronized event timestamps is unknown
No live service access is supplied

raw_candidates.claim: Stratifying counters by deployment interval might separate load-associated and release-associated explanations.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: The proposal compares predicted persistence under similar load across releases against predicted persistence within a release across load bands.
raw_candidates.discriminator: A release effect predicts a shift at comparable load; a load effect predicts a similar load relationship across releases. Neither pattern would defeat this discriminator's usefulness.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: inspect existing aggregate strata and document missing or confounded comparisons before assigning a cause.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Aggregate counters may conceal request mix; no causal attribution is established.

raw_candidates.claim: Aligning queue events and latency spikes could distinguish queue buildup from a downstream stall.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Queue-first and downstream-first accounts predict different temporal orderings.
raw_candidates.discriminator: A reliable opposite ordering defeats each respective account; unresolved clock error defeats the proposed ordering test itself.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: first determine whether synchronized timestamps exist, then bound timing error and inspect ordering.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Synchronized timestamps are indispensable and their existence is unknown; no permission change is assumed.

raw_candidates.claim: Injecting a downstream delay might reproduce the suspected signature.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: A controlled delay is predicted to generate an ordering resembling the hypothesized stall.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Rejected because injection changes the service and breaches read-only investigation. Failure to reproduce would weaken, but not eliminate, the stall account.
raw_candidates.probe: Parked; no injection is authorized by this packet.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Signature resemblance and transfer from a controlled perturbation remain untested.

packets.domain: analysis workflow: comparing defect causes across manufacturing shifts
packets.epistemic_status: Synthetic proposals only. No production records, measured defect rates, or causal findings are provided.

case.valued_outcome: Distinguish material-lot and shift-process explanations for a defect pattern.
resources: Hypothetical shift-level summaries and lot labels
Crossed lot-by-shift coverage is unknown
No additional sampling budget is supplied

raw_candidates.claim: A lot-by-shift comparison may distinguish the competing explanations when crossed records exist.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: A lot account predicts persistence across shifts; a process account predicts persistence across lots within the implicated shift.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Comparable crossed cells with the opposite pattern defeat each prediction. If coverage is confounded, the table cannot discriminate.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: inspect coverage and anonymous summaries, retaining absent cells as absent.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Discrimination depends on unknown coverage; the workflow can report non-identifiability while preserving constraints.

raw_candidates.claim: Collecting new crossed samples could reduce lot-shift confounding.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Deliberately crossed observations are predicted to expose differences hidden by existing assignments.
raw_candidates.discriminator: It predicts better separability, not a particular winning cause. Continued inseparability defeats its proposed advantage.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only after explicitly relaxing existing-records-only and obtaining a sampling resource.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Requires a stated hard-constraint relaxation; sampling access, expense, and discriminatory yield are also unknown.

raw_candidates.claim: Imputing empty cells might produce a complete comparison matrix.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Model assumptions would generate estimates where observations are absent.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Rejected because missing values must remain unimputed. A complete-looking matrix would not itself defeat confounding.
raw_candidates.probe: Parked; no imputation is proposed for execution.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Bias introduced by imputation and stability of any ranking remain unknown.

packets.domain: hammer-like design: reseating an overhead clip

case.valued_outcome: Reseat an overhead clip while maintaining a secure one-hand grip.
hard_constraints: One hand must operate and retain the device
resources: Clip geometry is hypothetical
A captive-head concept is available as a drawing only
Existence of a compatible elastomer latch material is unknown

raw_candidates.claim: A thumb-actuated captive plunger might reseat the clip.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: A guided head is predicted to keep the impulse along the clip axis and retain moving parts.
raw_candidates.discriminator: The source predicts adequate seating but makes no performance ordering against the spring latch. Failure to seat, loss of grip, or wiring contact defeats adequacy.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: exercise orientations on a wiring surrogate and assess seating, retention, and grip.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Available thumb force and guidance tolerance are unresolved.

raw_candidates.claim: A captive spring head held by an elastomer latch may deliver a repeatable tap.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Stored spring energy is predicted to reduce dependence on thumb speed.
raw_candidates.discriminator: It predicts less tap-to-tap variation than the plunger, without predicting higher seating success. Equivalent or greater variation defeats that comparative prediction.
raw_candidates.probe: Proposed only: establish compatible latch material availability, then compare repeated strokes on a surrogate.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: The indispensable latch material and its release stability are unknown; hard constraints remain in force.

raw_candidates.claim: Dropping a small unattached weight onto the clip might seat it.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Gravity is predicted to supply the impact energy.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Rejected because the weight can fall as a detached part. A successful seat would not remove this violation.
raw_candidates.probe: Parked; no overhead trial proposed.
raw_candidates.uncertainty: Whether it supplies enough energy and whether it contacts wiring are both unresolved.

resources: Hypothetical anonymous responses and original category labels

raw_candidates.claim: Mapping disagreements to definition boundaries might identify ambiguity clusters.
raw_candidates.causal_relation: Definition ambiguity predicts concentration near overlapping descriptions; application inconsistency predicts disagreement beyond those boundaries as well.
raw_candidates.discriminator: Disagreement well outside documented overlaps weakens the ambiguity-only account. A boundary cluster does not by itself exclude inconsistent application.

raw_candidates.uncertainty: Independent coders are indispensable and unavailable status is unknown; no new response collection is assumed.
